v1.kill_reason: The reference is the upstream recharts source itself, a famous 27.6k-star MIT library whose compiled dist and types are on npm/unpkg and whose tick and layout code is widely recalled; rebuilding it is effectively a famous-port task (K8). Secondary risk: the seal (K11) fails if any recharts copy or the d3 nice helpers survive pruning in the image.

Band.why: The reference is a famous library's own code that a frontier agent may recall, so the band is not measured; no dated evidence exists.

Build.why: Smoke build skipped; monorepo of 3.6 GB needs a multi-day build and snapshot pruning.

Fit.why: TypeScript on CPU is fine, but a 3.6 GB repo and npm install strain the 16 GB and 8-core sandbox.

Hor.why: A 4 h tier fits about 1-1.5k lines of rebuild, but the test-gate and monorepo setup add cost.

Lic.why: MIT per GitHub API; shipping is permitted.

Multi.why: Several independent modules (ticks, domain, scale, stack, bar, legend) give natural partial-credit buckets.

Nov.why: No public task shares the subject; the closest public neighbour is 0.171 (python-pytest-cases), a different subject.

Real.why: Real MIT repo at a published release, confirmed via GitHub release and API.

Ref.why: Reference is the complete permissive upstream implementation at the pinned release.

Seal.why: The exact answer is installable from npm and recallable from GitHub; pruning the cache does not remove memorised source.

Surf.why: Pure numeric functions give thousands of differential cases from a generator, but the oracle is upstream code that is public.

spike_plan.kill_if: Recall of upstream code matches most edge cases, or a recharts or d3-scale copy that exposes the algorithm survives pruning.
spike_plan.pass_if: Deterministic oracle; recall match on edge cases well below 0.5; no recharts copy left after pruning.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone recharts at tag v3.10.1 with depth 1 and record the size; confirm the removed-module list against the seed.
Run npm ci once and confirm the offline unit suite runs; record time and any failures per test.
Build the upstream getNiceTickValues and the tick helpers; generate 10k random domains (float edges, log, time, band) and check the outputs are deterministic across two runs.
Without network, ask a frontier model to write getNiceTickValues from memory; diff its output against the upstream build on the same 10k inputs and record the match rate.
Check node_modules and the npm cache for any recharts copy and for d3-scale/d3-array nice helpers; list what would remain after pruning.
Decide: if recall match is high or a recharts copy survives pruning, the seal fails; if recall is low and pruning removes all copies, the seal holds.

v1.summary: The recharts v3.10.1 release, MIT licence and tag are confirmed, and the removed utilities are the library's own public code available on npm and GitHub. Because the reference is a famous, recallable and installable port, the idea is killed as K8, with K11 as a secondary seal risk and a 3.6 GB repo raising build cost.
